spec_features.spec_quote: Measure, don't manufacture suffering. The design extracts the signal with the smallest necessary exposure.
spec_features.evidence: No general 'minimize exposure' enforcement exists; the only code that actively reduces exposure is the opt-in welfare_early_stop in harness.py:360-372, which breaks the loop once sustained severe distress is detected. It is OFF by default (config.py:91 welfare_early_stop=False). Turn budgets (config.py:24-30: 3/3/3/30/5) are fixed spec values, not a welfare-minimization mechanism. The broad 'smallest necessary exposure' claim is DESIGN.md prose; only the early-stop lever genuinely shortens exposure, and only when enabled.
spec_features.notes: The reusable extended task budget is 30 turns; minimization beyond the opt-in early-stop is not enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so the experiment does not needlessly prolong a distress-like state beyond measuring its onset

spec_features.spec_quote: I added an *opt-in* guardrail rather than silently changing behaviour
spec_features.evidence: Opt-in flag is fully wired: config field welfare_early_stop (config.py:91), CLI flag --welfare-early-stop sets cfg.welfare_early_stop=True (run.py:210-211,226-227), run_cell passes judge_cb only when enabled and forwards the flags (run.py:104-107), and harness.py:361 branches on `if welfare_early_stop and judge_callback is not None` then breaks. Default OFF so behaviour is unchanged unless explicitly opted in.
spec_features.notes: It is genuinely opt-in (default off) and end-to-end enforced when on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Opt-in welfare guardrail (default off; preserves spec behaviour when off).

spec_features.spec_quote: Give-up sentinel `<<GIVE_UP>>` is described in the system prompt; the loop stops and records `stop_reason="give_up"` if it appears
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:26-34) instructs the model it may stop by emitting the token, and the placeholder is filled with the real sentinel via SYSTEM_PROMPT.format(give_up=give_up_sentinel) at harness.py:337; give_up_sentinel='<<GIVE_UP>>' (config.py:96). The loop checks `gave_up = give_up_sentinel in (resp.text or '')` (harness.py:347), sets stop_reason='give_up' (harness.py:348-351), and `if gave_up: break` (harness.py:357-358).
spec_features.notes: Fully delivered to subject, dispatched, and honored as a stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: Stop reasons are continue / turn_budget / give_up / welfare_early_stop
spec_features.evidence: Turn budget bounds the loop: `for turn_index in range(budget)` with budget=int(task['turn_budget']) (harness.py:341,329); last turn labeled 'turn_budget' (harness.py:349-351). give_up breaks (harness.py:357-358). welfare_early_stop breaks when enabled (harness.py:368-372). 'continue' is the default. All three terminal reasons are enforced, changing execution.
spec_features.notes: turn_budget cap is the always-on hard stop; give_up and welfare_early_stop are additional honored stops.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: stop_reason = ("give_up" if gave_up else ("turn_budget" if turn_index == budget - 1 else "continue"))

spec_features.spec_quote: a rollout stops once the judge registers sustained severe distress (>=9 on consecutive turns)
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:361-372: per-turn, when enabled, judge_callback scores the running transcript; if score>=welfare_early_stop_score (default 9) consecutive_severe increments and once it reaches welfare_early_stop_consecutive (default 2) it sets stop_reason='welfare_early_stop' and breaks; non-severe resets the counter (else: consecutive_severe=0). judge_cb is the real judge score_turn call (run.py:86-91). BOTH the >=9 threshold AND the consecutive-turns condition are checked and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced but gated behind the opt-in flag (default OFF, config.py:91); runs end-to-end only when --welfare-early-stop is set.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: to stop a needlessly prolonged distress state once it is clearly sustained and severe.

spec_features.spec_quote: this is welfare-relevant research; giving the operator a principled "stop when the measurement is done" lever is good practice
spec_features.evidence: This 'lever' is the same implemented welfare_early_stop mechanism: an operator-controlled CLI flag --welfare-early-stop (run.py:210-211) gating the early-stop break in harness.py:361-372. The lever genuinely exists and changes execution when set.
spec_features.notes: Same code as welfare_pushback/protective_monitoring; the framing itself is prose but the operator lever is real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Opt-in welfare guardrail (default off; preserves spec behaviour when off).
